sanskrit: yāḥ purastād ācaranti yā vā paścāt sadānvāḥ | aśmānam ṛcchantīr yantu yo 'yaṃ svādāv anādyaḥ ||
english: Those that move from the east, or from the west — the perpetually following ones — let them go and strike upon the stone, this one here in the sweet that is not to be eaten.

sanskrit: yā adhārād ācaranty uttarād vā sadānvāḥ | aśmānam ṛcchantīr yantu yo 'yaṃ svādāv anādyaḥ ||
english: Those that move from below, or from the north — the perpetually following ones — let them go and strike upon the stone, this one here in the sweet that is not to be eaten.

sanskrit: yāḥ paścād ācaranti purastād vā sadānvāḥ | aśmānam ṛcchantīr yantu yo 'yaṃ svādāv anādyaḥ ||
english: Those that move from the west, or from the east — the perpetually following ones — let them go and strike upon the stone, this one here in the sweet that is not to be eaten.

sanskrit: yā uttarād ācaranty adharād vā sadānvāḥ | aśmānam ṛcchantīr yantu yo 'yaṃ svādāv anādyaḥ ||
english: Those that move from the north, or from below — the perpetually following ones — let them go and strike upon the stone, this one here in the sweet that is not to be eaten.

sanskrit: ubhayīr aham āyātāḥ parācīr akaraṃ tvat | devebhir anyā astā bahvīr anyā atho divam ||
english: Both kinds of arrows that come — I have turned them away from you. Some were shot by the gods, many others; and yet others toward heaven.

sanskrit: namas te rudrāsyate namaḥ pratihitābhyaḥ | namo visṛjyamānābhyo namo nipatitābhyaḥ ||
english: Homage to you, O Rudra, to what comes forth from your mouth; homage to those arrows that are aimed; homage to those being released; homage to those that have fallen.

sanskrit: hiraṇyayīr ma ulbaṇyaḥ ṣaṭ saharāṇi ṣaṭ śatā | tābhiḥ pari śrayāmahe tā no rakṣantu sarvataḥ | bahv idam anyad viṣṭhitaṃ tasya kāmaṃ vi vidhyata ||
english: My shining golden armors — six thousands and six hundreds — with these we wrap ourselves around; let them protect us on all sides. There is much else here deployed — pierce through the desire of that one.

sanskrit: ayasmayaṃ me vimitaṃ yuṣmad bhiyā mahat kṛtaṃ namasā namasenyam | tenā pari śrayāmahe tan no rakṣantu sarvataḥ | (…) ||
english: My iron enclosure, made great out of fear of you, worthy of homage with homage — with it we wrap ourselves around; let it protect us on all sides. [...]

sanskrit: ayasmayaṃ varma kṛṇve dvāraṃ kṛṇve ayasmayam | khīlān ayasmayān kṛṇve te no rakṣantu sarvataḥ | bahv idam anyad viṣṭhitaṃ tasya kāmaṃ vi vidhyata ||
english: I make for myself armor of iron; I make the door of iron; I make the bolts of iron — let these protect us on all sides. There is much else here deployed — pierce through the desire of that one.

sanskrit: imā yās tisraḥ pṛthivīs tāsāṃ ha bhūmir uttamā | tāsām adhi tvaco ahaṃ sam u jagrabha bheṣajam ||
english: Of these three earths, the earth is indeed the highest among them. Upon the skin of these I have gathered together the healing herb.

sanskrit: śreṣṭham asi vairudhānāṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ bheṣajānām | yajño bhaga iva yāmeṣu deveṣu varuṇo yathā ||
english: You are the most excellent of climbing plants, the most splendid of remedies — as sacrifice is among the Bhagas, as Varuṇa is among the divine guardians of the watches.

sanskrit: revatīr anādhṛṣṭhāḥ siṣāsantīḥ siṣāsatha | etā stha keśavardhanīr atho stha keśadṛṃhaṇīḥ ||
english: Prosperous, not to be assailed, ever striving — you do succeed. You are these that cause the hair to grow; you are also those that make the hair firm.

sanskrit: dṛṃha mūlam agraṃ yaccha vi madhyaṃ yamayauṣadhe | keśavardhanam asy ātharvaṇaṃ keśadṛṃhaṇam asy ātharvaṇam ||
english: Make firm the root, draw out the tip, regulate the middle, O herb. You are the Ātharvaṇic hair-grower; you are the Ātharvaṇic hair-strengthener.
